subject.title: fix(openshell): mirror sandboxes can modify workspace skill files despite read-only policy

question: Should a sandbox/security owner approve this exact OpenShell mirror enforcement policy after a fresh source-based review of the rebased head?
rationale: The requested behavior narrows what a writable sandbox can persist into the host workspace. The supplied evidence is promising, but the required direct comparison of the exact implementation with current sibling policy could not be performed in this environment.

options.title: Refresh and approve the boundary
options.body: Rebase or refresh the PR, then have a sandbox/security owner verify both protected-root seams against current Docker and remote-bridge behavior before merge.

options.title: Pause for a narrower policy design
options.body: Pause the PR if maintainers want a shared core seam for protected skill roots instead of keeping equivalent OpenShell-specific enforcement.

recommendation.title: Refresh and approve the boundary
recommendation.body: Rebase or refresh the PR, then have a sandbox/security owner verify both protected-root seams against current Docker and remote-bridge behavior before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged related sandbox-skill work is the strongest available ownership signal for the protected-root policy.
